# Terrain

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("Terrain")`

A sculpted landscape that collides: ground that you dig into and build up, instead of a floor made of parts.

Terrain is a grid of voxels. Space is divided into cubes `VoxelSize` on a side. Each voxel holds a material and an occupancy, which is how full of that material it is, from 0 to 1. The surface lies where the occupancy crosses one half, interpolated between neighboring voxels, so the ground is smooth and not stepped. Caves, arches, overhangs and flat ground are all the same data.

Materials are numbered. 0 is air, and `n` is the terrain's layer `n`, a material asset (see `GetLayers`). A new terrain has no layers and draws plain gray ground until `SetLayers` gives it some.

A `Workspace` has one terrain, `workspace.Terrain`. You can create another, but the workspace does not refer to it.

Every editing method writes voxels, and voxels are part of the world: an edit can be undone in the editor and is saved with the project.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CellCount` | `number` | — | read-only | The number of 32 by 32 by 32 voxel chunks that currently hold any ground. Air is not stored, so the count is 0 for an empty terrain. |
| `CellSize` | `number` | `64` | read-only, **stored, not yet acted on** | The width of one streamed cell of terrain, in meters. It is the spacing of the world's streaming grid.<br><br>A terrain saved with a scene that spans 256 cells or more is divided into cells of this size, rounded to whole columns of 32-voxel chunks. Each cell is loaded and unloaded around the focuses of `StreamingService`, at its terrain radii. A cell that was changed during a run is written to the run's cache on disk when it is unloaded, and loads again with the change. |
| `MaxHeight` | `number` | `256` | read/write | The highest height, in meters, at which a voxel can be written. |
| `MinHeight` | `number` | `-256` | read/write | The lowest height, in meters, at which a voxel can be written.<br><br>Ground created where there was none, by `WriteHeights`, by the editor's Generate Flat Ground or by raising empty terrain, is a slab 32 meters deep below its lowest surface, rounded down to a whole chunk and never below this height. |
| `Position` | `vector` | `vector.zero` | read/write | The position of the terrain's origin in the world, in meters. Every voxel, collider and edit is offset by it, so moving a sculpted terrain is cheap. A terrain can be moved but not rotated. |
| `VoxelSize` | `number` | `1` | read/write | The size of one voxel, in meters, from 0.1 to 64. One meter resolves a doorway or a path. Two meters resolves a hillside and uses an eighth of the memory.<br><br>It can be set only while the terrain is empty. Call `Clear` first to change it on a sculpted terrain. |

## Methods

### `ApplyRules(minCorner: vector, maxCorner: vector): number`

Writes the materials that the rules draw into the surface voxels in the box between two corners. The rules can then be removed with no visible change. Returns the number of voxels it changed.

### `CellCenterToWorld(cell: vector): vector`

Returns the world position of the center of a voxel, given its index along each axis.

### `Clear()`

Removes every voxel. The terrain is then empty and `VoxelSize` can be set again.

### `Compact(): number`

Does nothing and returns 0. Terrain storage is always compact. The method is kept so that scripts that call it still run.

### `FillBall(center: vector, radius: number, material: number): number`

Adds a ball of ground, or removes one when `material` is 0. Returns the number of voxels it changed.

Adding never removes ground, and removing never adds it. A voxel ends up as full as the fuller of itself and the ball when adding, or as empty as the ball leaves it when removing. An explosion crater is `FillBall(hit.Position, 4, 0)`.

Raises an error for a position or size that is not a finite number, or for a negative radius. This applies to every `Terrain` method that edits or reads. A return value of 0 means the ground was already as requested, or the edit was entirely outside `MinHeight` to `MaxHeight`.

### `FillBlock(center: vector, size: vector, material: number): number`

Adds an axis-aligned box of ground `size` across, or removes one when `material` is 0. Returns the number of voxels it changed.

### `FillCylinder(center: vector, height: number, radius: number, material: number): number`

Adds an upright cylinder of ground `height` tall, or removes one when `material` is 0. Returns the number of voxels it changed. A well is `FillCylinder(top - vector.create(0, 10, 0), 20, 1.5, 0)`.

### `FlattenBall(center: vector, radius: number, height: number, strength: number?): number`

Pulls the ground in a ball toward a level plane at `height`, removing what is above the plane and filling what is below it. `strength` (0 to 1, default 1) sets how far, less toward the rim. Returns the number of voxels it changed.

### `GetLayers(): { string }`

Returns the terrain's layers: a list of material URNs in which entry `n` is the material that voxels of material `n` are drawn with. A new terrain has none.

A scene saved by a version of the engine in which terrains had built-in layers returns those eight, `engine://terrain/grass` to `engine://terrain/ice`.

### `GetRules(): { { Enabled: boolean, Material: number, SlopeMin: number, SlopeMax: number, HeightMin: number, HeightMax: number, Blend: number, Noise: number, AppliesTo: { number } } }`

Returns the rules that choose the ground's material by slope and height, in the order they are applied. A new terrain has none.

Each rule draws `Material` where the ground is between `SlopeMin` and `SlopeMax` degrees and between `HeightMin` and `HeightMax` meters. `AppliesTo` lists the layers it draws over; an empty list means every layer except its own. `Blend` is the width of its edge, in degrees or meters, and `Noise` is how irregular the edge is.

Rules change what is drawn, not the voxels: the voxels keep their materials until `ApplyRules`. A raycast reports the material that is drawn.

### `GrowBall(center: vector, radius: number, amount: number, material: number?): number`

Moves the surface near `center` outward along its own slope by `amount` meters at the middle, falling smoothly to nothing at `radius`. A negative `amount` moves it inward. Returns the number of voxels it changed.

This is what the editor's Raise and Lower tools do: a field rises, a cliff moves forward, and an overhang grows downward. New ground is made of `material`, or of the neighboring ground's material when none is given.

### `HeightAt(x: number, z: number): number?`

Returns the height of the top of the ground at a position, in meters, or nil where there is no ground.

The result is the highest surface in the column, even above a cave. That is where to plant a tree or where a player lands from above. For the first surface along a direction, use `Workspace:Raycast`.

It also returns nil where the ground has not streamed in yet. In a large world, wait for the area with `StreamingService:LoadAreaAsync(position, radius)` first.

### `IsMeshed(center: vector, radius: number): boolean`

Returns whether the ground within `radius` of `center` is drawn in its final form. That means every piece the view needs there has its mesh built and uploaded at the detail it will be drawn at, and no further refinement is pending.

Ground that a script has just written exists at once and is meshed a few frames later; this method reports the second. The answer is as of the last frame drawn. It is always true where nothing is drawn, such as on a server or in a run with no camera.

### `PaintBall(center: vector, radius: number, material: number, options: { Mode: Enum.TerrainPaintMode?, Strength: number?, Falloff: number? }? = nil): number`

Changes the material of the ground in a ball without moving the surface. Returns the number of voxels it changed.

A voxel holds two materials, one over the other, and how much of the upper one shows. `options.Mode` chooses what the stroke does with them:

- `Replace`, the default, makes the ground `material` outright.
- `Blend` shows more of `material` over what is there, by `Strength` (0 to 1, default 1). `Falloff` is the share of the radius over which the stroke fades toward the rim: 0, the default, is a hard edge, 0.5 fades over the outer half, and 1 fades from the center.
- `Under` puts `material` under what was painted over it.
- `Erase` shows less of the upper material, revealing the one under it.

A `material` of 0 raises an error, except in `Erase` mode, which takes no material.

### `RaiseBall(center: vector, radius: number, amount: number, material: number?): number`

Raises the ground around `center` by `amount` meters at the middle, falling smoothly to nothing at `radius`. A negative `amount` lowers it. Returns the number of voxels it changed.

It moves the existing surface instead of adding a ball. The ground within `radius` above and below `center` is pushed up, so a hill rises with no overhang at its rim, and a tunnel farther down stays where it is. Use it to shape hills and valleys; use `FillBall` for a boulder or a tunnel.

Where a column within reach has no ground and `material` is given, raising creates new ground of that material from the height of `center` upward.

### `ReadVoxels(minCorner: vector, maxCorner: vector): ({ number }, { number }, vector)`

Returns the voxels in the box between two corners, snapped outward to the grid. The results are their materials, their occupancies (0 to 1) and the number of voxels along each axis.

The two tables are flat. The voxel at `x, y, z`, counted from 0 at the low corner, is at index `1 + x + size.X * (y + size.Y * z)`. One call reads at most 256 voxels along each axis; read a larger region in pieces.

### `ReplaceMaterial(minCorner: vector, maxCorner: vector, from: number, to: number): number`

Changes every voxel of material `from` to material `to` in the box between two corners. Returns the number of voxels it changed. Raises an error if either material is 0: this method changes what the ground is made of, not whether it is there.

### `SetLayers(layers: { string })`

Sets the terrain's layers, in the form that `GetLayers` returns: up to 255 material URNs, entry `n` for material `n`. Voxels keep their numbers, so replacing entry 3 changes every voxel of material 3 at once. To paint with a new material, add it at the end. Layers are saved with the scene.

### `SetRules(rules: { { read Enabled: boolean?, read Material: number?, read SlopeMin: number?, read SlopeMax: number?, read HeightMin: number?, read HeightMax: number?, read Blend: number?, read Noise: number?, read AppliesTo: { number }? } })`

Sets the terrain's rules, in the form that `GetRules` returns: up to 16, applied in order. A field left out takes its default: `Enabled` true, slopes 0 to 90, no height limits, `Blend` 10 and `Noise` 0.12. An empty list removes all rules. Rules are saved with the scene.

### `SmoothBall(center: vector, radius: number, strength: number?): number`

Smooths the ground in a ball. Each point of the surface moves toward the average of the surface around it by `strength` (0 to 1, default 0.5), less toward the rim. Returns the number of voxels it changed.

Flat ground does not move, and a slab is never cut through. Material removed from a bump is spread around it, so the volume of ground stays nearly constant over repeated strokes. The average is taken over a width of half the brush, at most four voxels.

### `WaitForMeshAsync(center: vector, radius: number, timeout: number? = 30): boolean`

This method yields: the calling thread waits until it completes.

Yields until `IsMeshed(center, radius)` is true and returns true, or returns false after `timeout` seconds of simulation time. Use it in a loading screen after building a terrain, before letting the player in. Together with `SceneService:HoldLoading`, it keeps the engine's loading screen up until the ground is ready.

### `WorldToCell(position: vector): vector`

Returns the voxel that a world position falls in, as its integer index along each axis.

### `WriteHeights(corner: vector, columns: number, heights: { number }, material: (number | { number })?): number`

Writes a heightmap in one call: one height per column of voxels, `columns` to a row, row after row along +Z, starting at the column that `corner` falls in. Only the X and Z of `corner` are used. Returns the number of voxels it changed.

Use it for ground that comes from data, such as generated noise or an image, where one brush call per column would be far too slow. Heights are in meters in world space and are clamped between `MinHeight` and `MaxHeight`. A height that is not a number is skipped.

`material` (default 1) is what new ground is made of: one id for all of it, or a table of ids parallel to `heights`, in which 0 leaves that column unchanged.

The top of each column moves to its height: ground is added from the old top upward or removed from it downward, and a cave below the top is kept. A column with no ground at all is created as a slab 32 meters deep below the lowest height in the table.

### `WriteVoxels(corner: vector, size: vector, materials: { number }, occupancies: { number }): number`

Writes a box of voxels in one call, in the layout that `ReadVoxels` returns. `corner` is a point in the first voxel, `size` is the number of voxels along each axis, and each table holds one entry per voxel. Returns the number of voxels it changed.

A material of 0 or an occupancy of 0 is air. Writing what `ReadVoxels` returned restores the terrain exactly. Use it to copy a piece of terrain, to generate terrain voxel by voxel, or to undo a script's own change.
